summary: Streaming socket unexpectedly closes after interleaved keepalive + proxy timeout during long generation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports streaming chat sessions disconnecting silently or closing with network error during long-generation responses (>30s). This happens intermittently for ~4 customers on the same Dedicated pool. Impact: user-visible mid-generation disconnects causing partial responses and retries in the client.

Impact:
- NoteRight web app: ~2-3% of streaming requests for long prompts are dropped mid-generation, resulting in truncated assistant responses.
- Customer has dedicated capacity; they see no worker OOMs but observe worker reassignments around the time of failures.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-us-east-07 (3 GPU workers per zone), autoscaler enabled with aggressive downscale (idle_timeout=60s).
- Customer uses SSE streaming via our public API through their VPC NAT and an internal nginx reverse proxy on their side.

Expected behavior:
- Long streaming responses should deliver SSE chunks continuously until final token or explicit [DONE] event; keepalive pings should not trigger connection close.

Observed behavior:
- SSE channel becomes silent for 3–8s mid-generation, then client receives a TCP/WS close (1006) or SSE connection reset. No final [DONE] event.

Attachments: customer-provided pcap, app logs, and a short screen capture.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer issues a streaming chat request using redwood/gptx-13b-v1 with a 4k token prompt and stream=true.
2) Server begins sending tokens as SSE events.
3) After ~18–45s, stream pauses for several seconds, then closes without final chunk.
4) Client reports socket error 1006 or HTTP/2 stream reset.

Notes: Repro rate is ~1 in 30 long requests in their traffic pattern; more likely during bursty traffic when autoscaler is active.
logs:
Excerpt from customer's SSE stream (sanitized):

[data: {"token":"The model continues with ..."}]
[data: {"token":"... further text ..."}]

<silence for 6.2s>

[Connection closed by peer: ECONNRESET]

Agent logs from worker-12 (serving-runtime):
2026-03-09T14:21:37.112Z INFO kv-cache: refresh prefix for session=abc123
2026-03-09T14:21:43.879Z WARN autoscaler: evicting idle worker worker-12 (scale-down)
2026-03-09T14:21:43.980Z INFO runtime: finishing in-flight request id=req-987 (graceful-handoff)
2026-03-09T14:21:44.005Z ERROR connection: upstream socket closed unexpectedly (code=1006)

Proxy logs (customer nginx):
2026/03/09 10:21:44 [info] 23456#0: *524 idle timeout, client: 10.0.12.45, server: note-right, request: "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1"
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses considered:
- Client-side proxy (nginx) keepalive or buffer coalescing dropping SSE after short silence.
- Autoscaler scale-down evicting a worker that was actively serving a long stream; handoff timing causes socket to close.
- Intermediate LB/TCP timeout or TLS session renegotiation leading to abrupt close.

What we've done so far:
- Replayed request in staging against identical model; reproduced a quiet window when we artificially triggered a worker scale-down.
- Correlated timestamps: autoscaler evict event in runtime logs aligns within 100–200ms of connection close in several samples.
- Verified serving-runtime returns graceful-handoff code path, but client still sees underlying socket close. Worker logs show "finishing in-flight request" followed by immediate socket tear-down for SSE path.
- Reviewed nginx keepalive settings on customer's side; they have proxy_read_timeout default (60s) but observed close happens well before 60s. Customer uses an external load balancer with connection tracking that reports an idle close at ~30s.
- Temporary mitigation: increased autoscaler idle_timeout from 60s -> 180s in a dedicated pool replica; customer reports drop rate fell to near 0 in 24h smoke test.

Open questions:
- Why graceful-handoff is not maintaining socket when the worker is evicted for streaming (SSE/WS) paths?
- Are we failing to attach the upstream socket to the new worker in time, or is there a gap where the proxy treats it as idle?
- Does KV cache refresh or prefix flush contribute to a temporary pause that triggers LB idle detection?
comments: Aisha Clarke (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports ~2.3% mid-stream disconnect rate for long streams. Provided pcap and nginx logs. Escalating to SRE/serving-runtime. Slack thread: #support-suprt-843210

Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging by forcing scale-down during a long-running streamed request. Observed socket close even when runtime logs indicate graceful handoff. Opening runtime investigation. See GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3421 for a proposed fix to the handoff path.
Elena Park (Customer Success) 2026-03-11: Notified NoteRight that we are testing a mitigation (increase idle_timeout) on a mirrored pool; monitoring for 24h before rolling wider.

Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-12: Rolling patch deployed to staging that defers scale-down until streaming connections hand off. Need engineering sign-off before prod rollout. Linked INT-3682 for infra change.
NoteRight Support Contact (customer) 2026-03-12: Confirmed that after idle_timeout change we saw no disconnects in 24h sample (smoke test of ~400 long streams).
resolution:
Partial workaround: increase autoscaler idle_timeout for dedicated pools serving streaming-heavy workloads (customer applied 60s->180s and experienced immediate reduction in failures).

Root cause (provisional): aggressive autoscaler scale-down was evicting workers serving long SSE streams. Although the runtime enters a graceful-handoff code path for in-flight requests, the underlying connection handoff for streaming protocols was not fully preserved; intermediate LBs/proxies interpret the short silence during handoff as an idle connection and close it.

Next steps/actions:
- [Engineering] Finish PR #3421 to guarantee connection socket ownership transfer during graceful-handoff for streaming paths. (ETA: 2026-03-18).
- [SRE] Coordinate a graduated rollout of idle_timeout increase for affected dedicated pools until fix is live.
- [Support] Add guidance to Support KB: "Dedicated pools + streaming: recommended autoscaler idletime >= 120s".
- [Customer Success] Follow up with NoteRight in 7 days to confirm stability and discuss whether to keep the idle_timeout change long-term or wait for runtime fix.

Status: In Progress (temporary mitigation applied; engineering fix in PR).
